article.title: NFL EDGE Sunday Morning Brief
article.dek: Sunday's slate is here, the morning board changes two of the three cards, and the Saturday injury news still sets the table — with the inactive lists as the one thing left to wait for.

items.headline: Lead: the morning board changes two cards — and Sunday's games are here
paragraphs: The morning board changes two of the three cards from Saturday evening. Balanced is now Chicago +3 at -102 at FanDuel for Monday night at Seattle, and Value is now Denver +1.5 at -112 at FanDuel for Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET against Kansas City. Hit Rate stays the Los Angeles Rams moneyline, now -258 at DraftKings for Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET against the Chargers.

That is the board as it stands this morning. The 1:00 p.m. ET games kick off first: Arizona at Dallas, Atlanta at Tampa Bay, Baltimore at Buffalo, Cleveland at Pittsburgh, Indianapolis at Jacksonville, Las Vegas at the Jets, Minnesota at Detroit, and Tennessee at Cincinnati. The late games are the Chargers at the Rams, Kansas City at Denver, and New England at Miami, with Philadelphia at Washington at 8:20 p.m. ET tonight.

One thing is still to come, and it is the only thing worth waiting for: the inactive lists, about 90 minutes before each kickoff, for the questionable names below. Check them before you lock anything in.
items.takeaway: Two cards change on the morning board — Chicago is the new Balanced pick and Denver the new Value pick — and the inactive lists are the last update before kickoff.

items.headline: Injury roundup: Saturday's designations carry into Sunday
paragraphs: Kansas City goes to Denver without two cornerbacks. The Chiefs placed L'Jarius Sneed on injured reserve Saturday and downgraded rookie Mansoor Delane to out with a shoulder injury. The Chargers placed safety Derwin James on injured reserve Saturday after a hamstring setback, pushing his earliest return to Week 12, and ruled out guard Kayode Awosika, defensive back Deane Leonard and receiver Brenen Thompson for Sunday against the Rams.

New England goes to Miami without receiver A.J. Brown (ankle) and running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness), both ruled out Saturday. Friday's clearances still stand: Lamar Jackson is cleared for Baltimore at Buffalo, and Saquon Barkley is cleared for Philadelphia at Washington.

The outs from Friday's final reports still stand too: Philadelphia is without DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Jihaad Campbell, Britain Covey and Jonathan Jones. Washington is without starting defensive lineman Javon Kinlaw. Baltimore is without Vega Ioane and Jaylinn Hawkins, and Denver ruled out running back RJ Harvey.

The questionables to carry into Sunday: Buffalo's DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid, Philadelphia's Jakorian Bennett, Washington's Daron Payne, John Bates, Treylon Burks and Jer'Zhan Newton, and Denver's Jaylen Waddle (chest) and Garett Bolles (hip). Monday night has its own report: Chicago ruled out running back Kyle Monangai (toe), and Seattle ruled out receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee). Questionable does not mean out — the inactive lists about 90 minutes before kickoff are the next real update.
items.takeaway: The Saturday outs and clearances stand, the questionables carry into Sunday, and the inactive lists are the next real update.

items.headline: Weather: calm and dry across Sunday's outdoor games
paragraphs: Sunday's outdoor games get a calm, dry forecast. In Buffalo, the National Weather Service calls for 67 degrees at the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff against Baltimore, mostly sunny skies, a 6 mph south wind and a 2 percent chance of precipitation.
In Denver, Sunday afternoon looks mostly cloudy with temperatures in the low 60s around the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff against Kansas City, a light south-southeast wind and only a small rain chance.

In Landover for Sunday night, the National Weather Service hourly forecast has about 51 degrees at the 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff between Philadelphia and Washington, a near-calm south wind, zero percent rain chance, and temperatures falling to about 50 degrees as the game goes on.
That is the forecast as it stands Sunday morning, reported as fact. It is not a reason to bet a total one way or the other.
items.takeaway: Buffalo: 67 and mostly sunny. Denver: low 60s, small rain chance. Landover: about 51 at kickoff, falling to about 50, no rain.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Morning cards: Rams still on top for likelihood, Chicago and Denver join the board
paragraphs: Hit Rate is the Los Angeles Rams moneyline at -258 at DraftKings, Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET against the Chargers. It is the pick the app rates most likely to win, with a model probability of 0.649. Remember the app's own tutorial: Hit Rate is not Profit Rate. A heavy moneyline favorite can look safe and still pay very little — you are betting on the outright winner only.
Balanced is Chicago +3 at -102 at FanDuel, Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET at Seattle. It is a strong pick without paying too much — the middle ground, and a good starting point for a new bettor.
Value is Denver +1.5 at -112 at FanDuel, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET against Kansas City. Value is always the model's +EV play. The app rates it at a model probability of 0.506.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate: Rams moneyline -258. Balanced: Chicago +3 -102 at FanDuel. Value: Denver +1.5 -112 at FanDuel.

items.headline: A card that changes still means checking your own price
paragraphs: The cards above are priced at DraftKings and FanDuel. If your book is neither, the card price is not your price.

Tap Check in the app, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. That is a full re-evaluation, not a blind override.

Odds are price mechanics: -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. The app sets your actual stake from your bankroll and staking setting — that part is deliberately conservative, and it lives in the app, not here.
items.takeaway: Your book's price is the one that matters — run it through Check and let that verdict decide.

items.headline: Learn the Game: handle versus tickets
paragraphs: Two numbers describe where the betting money sits: handle and tickets. Handle is the share of dollars wagered. Tickets is the share of individual bets placed. They often point the same way, but when they split, they tell different stories.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say 70 percent of the tickets are on the favorite, but only 40 percent of the handle is. That means lots of smaller bets on the favorite and fewer, larger bets on the underdog. It does not prove the underdog wins — it just tells you the big money and the crowd disagree, and that is worth noticing before you follow the crowd.
That is the whole idea behind a Fade: not a command to bet against the public, but a second look at a price when the money and the crowd are not on the same side.
items.takeaway: Handle is the share of dollars, tickets is the share of bets — when they disagree, the crowd and the big money are telling different stories.

items.headline: Morning board vs evening board: two card changes, one price improves
paragraphs: The morning board changes two cards. Balanced moves from Baltimore +3 at -104 at FanDuel to Chicago +3 at -102 at FanDuel, with a play-through price of -105. Value moves from Chicago +3 at -105 at DraftKings to Denver +1.5 at -112 at FanDuel, with a play-through price of -113. Those are recommendation replacements, not price moves on the same pick — the old picks are off the board this morning.

The one pick that stays also gets cheaper. Hit Rate, the Rams moneyline, improves from -265 to -258 at DraftKings, with the play-through price moving from -269 to -262. Same pick, cheaper than it was Saturday evening.
The morning refresh caught all of it. If your book shows something different from the prices above, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and let the app re-evaluate it for you.
items.takeaway: Two card changes — Chicago replaces Baltimore as Balanced, Denver replaces Chicago as Value — and the Rams moneyline improves to -258.

items.headline: Sunday job: wait for one thing only, then trust Check
paragraphs: There is one piece of information worth waiting for: the inactive lists, about 90 minutes before each kickoff, for the questionable names above. That is a real pending event with a set time.
Everything else is ready now. If your book has a good number and Check says bet, bet now — waiting for the Sunday rush lets the number drift the wrong way too, especially on big-name teams.

One more habit for the weekend: settlement in the app is manual, and the tracker only works if you are honest with yourself. Log the losers too. A tracker that only holds winners is not a record, it is a highlight reel.
items.takeaway: Wait only for Sunday's inactive lists; otherwise bet when Check says bet — and log every result, winners and losers alike.

evidence.fact: The Kansas City Chiefs placed cornerback L'Jarius Sneed on injured reserve Saturday, Oct. 31, and downgraded rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane to out for Sunday's game at Denver with a shoulder injury. Sneed sits at least four games (Denver, Jets, Falcons, Cardinals). Both had been listed questionable. Delane, the No. 6 overall pick in the 2026 draft, had an on-and-off shoulder problem for months.

The Los Angeles Chargers placed safety Derwin James on injured reserve Saturday, Oct. 31, after a hamstring setback in his return from the hamstring injury that sidelined him since Week 3; earliest return Week 12 vs New England. The Chargers also ruled out G Kayode Awosika (fibula), DB Deane Leonard (concussion) and WR Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) for Sunday vs the Rams; CBs Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley are questionable; WR Ladd McConkey is expected to play after full practices following a Monday concussion absence.

New England Patriots WR A.J. Brown (ankle) was limited Wednesday, downgraded to DNP Thursday and Friday, and ruled out for Week 8 at Miami. Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was ruled out Saturday after missing practice Wednesday and Thursday.

Friday's final injury reports still stand Saturday evening: Baltimore QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) carries no game designation and head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Friday Jackson will play Sunday at Buffalo; Philadelphia RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) carries no game designation for Sunday night at Washington. Philadelphia ruled out WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring), WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), LB Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), WR Britain Covey (knee) and CB Jonathan Jones (hamstring); CB Jakorian Bennett questionable (knee). Washington ruled out starting DL Javon Kinlaw; DL Daron Payne (foot), TE John Bates, WR Treylon Burks and DL Jer'Zhan Newton questionable. Buffalo listed WR DJ Moore and TE Dalton Kincaid questionable. Baltimore ruled out RG Vega Ioane (knee) and S Jaylinn Hawkins (knee). Denver ruled out RB RJ Harvey (knee); WR Jaylen Waddle (chest) and LT Garett Bolles (hip) questionable.

Chicago Bears final injury report for Monday night vs Seattle, filed Saturday: RB Kyle Monangai (toe) did not practice all week and is ruled out, his fourth straight missed game; CB Malik Muhammad (toe) and LB D'Marco Jackson (ankle) questionable; TE Colston Loveland (neck) removed from the injury report; LB T.J. Edwards (hamstring) returns.

Seattle Seahawks WR Rashid Shaheed (knee) was ruled out for Week 8 on Saturday. RB Zach Charbonnet (knee) was removed from the injury report Saturday but the team has yet to activate him from injured reserve.
